title: Habits
examples: What is the easiest way to start a new good habit?
Does my brain remember habits differently than new things?
Can I really break a habit if I try hard enough?

explain.say: Today we are learning about habits and how they work in your brain.
A cue is a trigger that tells your brain to start a habit.
A routine is the action you take after the cue appears.
The reward is the positive feeling that makes you want to repeat the loop.
To build a habit, you repeat the cue, routine, and reward cycle many times.
For a real-life example, brushing your teeth is a perfect habit loop.

faq.q: What is the difference between a habit and a choice?
faq.a: A habit is automatic, like tying your shoes every morning. A choice is something you think about before you do it.
asks: How are habits different from decisions?

faq.q: Can I make a bad habit into a good one?
faq.a: Yes, you can. You need to change the cue or the routine part of the loop.
asks: Is it possible to change a habit?
What if I want to stop doing something bad?

faq.q: Does the reward have to be physical?
faq.a: No, the reward can be mental, like feeling proud of yourself. It can also be social, like getting praise.
asks: Does the reward have to be something I eat?

faq.q: How long does it take to build a strong habit?
faq.a: It takes consistent practice over time. Some habits take weeks, while others take months to feel natural.
asks: Is there a magic number of days?
How long must I keep doing it?

faq.q: What happens when I skip a day?
faq.a: Skipping a day is normal, but it can weaken the habit loop. Just start again with the next cue.
asks: Can I lose a habit if I stop for a week?
What is the best way to restart a habit?

facts: Habits are patterns of behaviour that become automatic over time.
The brain uses a loop of cue, routine, and reward to automate actions.
Breaking a habit often means finding a new routine for an old cue.
Consistency is more important than intensity when building habits.

quiz.say: If you see your gym bag (Cue) and immediately start jogging (Routine) because you feel energized (Reward), what part of the loop is the gym bag?
quiz.why: The cue is the trigger that starts the whole process.

wrong.1: The routine is the action you actually perform, like jogging.
wrong.2: The reward is the feeling you get after you finish jogging.
wrong.3: Action is too general; the specific term is cue.

quiz.say: You always check your phone (Routine) when you sit down in a quiet room (Cue) because it makes you feel connected (Reward). What is the routine?
quiz.why: The routine is the specific action you perform after the cue.

wrong.1: The quiet room is the cue, not the action.
wrong.2: This feeling is the reward, not the action.
wrong.3: Sitting down is just part of the setting, not the main action.

quiz.say: To break the habit of snacking while watching TV, you need to change which part of the loop?
quiz.why: To stop the bad habit, you must replace the old action with a new one.

wrong.0: Changing the cue is hard because it's often environmental.
wrong.1: Increasing the reward only makes the bad habit stronger.
wrong.2: You cannot ignore the cycle; you must actively change one part.
